  "reasoning": "All 16 selected answers agree with their own captured Math Academy worked solutions and are mathematically correct. Its final selected answer remains correct. For q-117752, the cosecant period is 2\\pi/(1/6)=12\\pi. The secant range shifted up by 4 is (-\\infty,3]\\cup[5,\\infty), and the cosecant range multiplied by 2 is (-\\infty,-2]\\cup[2,\\infty). Positive secant coefficients give local maximum values D-A, yielding -3 and 3/2. Secant excludes arguments \\pi/2+n\\pi, or 90 degrees plus multiples of 180 degrees; solving gives the stated domains. The original line in q-72571 has slope 3/2, so the perpendicular slope is -2/3; through (5,1), its equation is 2x+3y=13. Both interval-selection graphs have discontinuities at -3 and 3, and their selected intervals avoid these points. For q-48293, f is continuous throughout [-1,2], including left continuity at 2. For q-105181, h is continuous throughout [1,4], including right continuity at 1. For q-105413, q is continuous throughout (-\\infty,2]. For q-48348, h is continuous throughout (-\\infty,-1]. Tangent has period \\pi/|B|, giving \\pi/2 and \\pi/3. No earlier submitted answers or grades were supplied; the MA evidence here consists entirely of each question's own captured worked solution.",
